PullRequest.Title: agentHost: Restrict automatic PR association
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- add an experiment-controlled `chat.agentHost.experimental.autoAttachPullRequests` setting, defaulting to `false` outside Stable
- when automatic association is disabled, limit branch-aware PR state to agent-recorded PR artifacts and PRs explicitly selected or created through session actions
- continue validating eligible candidates against the checked-out branch or exact HEAD commit before exposing Mark Ready, Merge, Auto-Merge, and Agent Merge actions
- extract candidate ordering, reconciliation, race handling, and GitHub matching into an owned `AgentHostPullRequestAssociationResolver`

## Behavior

- PRs created or reused through the Create PR action remain associated
- sessions created through the PR picker retain their selected PR as an explicit association
- PR references (`isArtifact: false`) remain visible but never become actionable
- newly added and removed artifacts, branch changes, setting changes, failed turns, and cancelled turns all trigger reconciliation
- an open candidate wins over closed candidates, then the most recently signaled eligible candidate wins
- lookup failures still apply the restricted candidate filter before being surfaced

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- targeted ESLint across all changed TypeScript files
- 202 focused unit tests covering schema, resolver policy, Git state integration, GitHub matching, turn lifecycle, and PR-picker provenance

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed fan-out, per-key-only sequencing, default resident-session cardinality, and exact network/subprocess call chain are all directly established. The proportion of sessions that are cold/unassociated is workload-dependent, affecting magnitude rather than the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Concurrent GitHub API requests and git rev-parse subprocesses
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The burst grows linearly with every resident session lacking a verified pull request. The default residency limit is 10 (and held/subscribed sessions can exceed it); each cold miss performs one branch GET, then a git rev-parse and a second commit-to-PR GET.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: A single setting or experiment flip can produce a burst of subprocess and network activity, consuming GitHub rate limit and contending with interactive repository work.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this diff there was no auto-attach setting listener, so a root configuration change did not trigger repository-wide pull-request discovery across resident sessions.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Changing this root setting now starts reconciliation independently for every materialized session with no aggregate concurrency limit.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added loop queues `_queuePullRequestLookup(sessionKey)` for every session as soon as `autoAttachPullRequests` changes; `_pullRequestSequencer` serializes only by session key, so all different sessions run concurrently.
Findings.Title: Bound pull-request reconciliation when the setting changes
Findings.Impact: With ten cold feature-branch sessions, enabling automatic association can immediately issue roughly ten concurrent branch lookups and, on misses, ten concurrent `git rev-parse` processes followed by ten more GitHub requests. This background burst can throttle GitHub requests and slow other git work.
Findings.Evidence: `getSessionUris()` enumerates all materialized session states; normal residency allows 10. `_queuePullRequestLookup` uses `SequencerByKey`, which provides no global limit. `resolveForCheckout` calls `findPullRequestByHeadBranch`; a miss calls `revParse('HEAD')` and `findPullRequestByHeadSha`. The OctoKit cache only revalidates an already-seen exact route and does not coalesce cold requests across distinct session branches.
Findings.Recommendation: Run setting-triggered reconciliation through a small shared limiter (and prioritize the active session), or lazily reconcile inactive sessions; preserve per-session sequencing while bounding aggregate GitHub and subprocess concurrency.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The before/after event filter and subprocess call path are direct, and the added tests explicitly require success, cancelled, and error outcomes. Exact wall-clock impact varies by repository size and cancellation/error frequency.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Git subprocess launches and repository filesystem I/O
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The added cost occurs once per non-coalesced cancelled or errored turn. A refresh launches at least `git status` and `git remote -v`, usually `symbolic-ref`, and may add push-remote and base-divergence probes; rapid events coalesce per session, but ordinary turns separated by more than the five-second throttle each pay again.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Cancelled and failed requests now leave several background git processes running, increasing CPU/I/O load and contention with user or agent git commands.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before the diff, cancelled and errored turns performed no GitHub-reference attachment and therefore did not call `refreshSessionGitState` or its git probes.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every started turn that ends in cancellation or error now invokes the same full attach path previously reserved for successful turns.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The condition changed from `turn.reason.kind === 'success'` to accepting every outcome except `rejected` and `localCommand`, newly invoking `attachSessionGitHubPullRequest` for `cancelled` and `error`.
Findings.Title: Avoid a full git refresh after every failed or cancelled turn
Findings.Impact: Users who cancel slow turns or retry repeated provider errors now incur a full repository-state probe after each outcome. Even when restricted-resolution caching or an existing branch association avoids all GitHub traffic, the git refresh still runs and can slow concurrent source-control operations in large repositories.
Findings.Evidence: `GitHubReferencesContribution.onTurnEnd` fire-and-forgets `attachSessionGitHubPullRequest`; that method unconditionally awaits `refreshSessionGitState` first. `refreshSessionGitState` calls `getSessionGitState`, whose implementation launches 3 initial git probes in parallel and additional branch probes as needed, then holds its per-session throttler for five seconds. Turn errors do not set `SessionLifecycle.Failed` (that lifecycle is for session creation failure), so the refresh is reachable.
Findings.Recommendation: Preserve reconciliation semantics without always refreshing the repository: track whether the turn changed PR artifacts or checkout-relevant state and skip unchanged failed/cancelled turns, or add a restricted reconciliation entry point that uses the already-recorded git state when only artifact metadata changed.

Scenarios.Scenario: A started agent turn ends successfully, is cancelled, or errors, and GitHub references are reconciled.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: `onTurnEnd` invokes attachment fire-and-forget, so reconciliation is off the chat-response critical path. Within the background task, git refresh must finish before pull-request lookup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Compute session git state using parallel `git status`, `git remote -v`, and usually `git symbolic-ref`, followed by optional push-remote and base-divergence probes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Approximately 2-6 git subprocesses per non-coalesced outcome for one session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Successful turns already paid this cost; cancelled and errored turns did not invoke attachment before this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the response critical path, but competes with user/agent source-control work and keeps background work active.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Look up a pull request by head branch; on a miss, resolve HEAD locally and query pull requests by exact commit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Warm verified association: zero requests. Cold unresolved branch: one GET; a miss can cause a second GET after one `git rev-parse`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This lookup ran after successful turns only.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the response critical path; contributes API traffic after failed/cancelled turns only when association caches cannot short-circuit.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of cancelled/errored turns separated enough to escape the five-second per-session throttle; one active session is typical, with multiple sessions possible.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Git refreshes coalesce per session with `ThrottlerByKey`, retaining at most the active and latest queued task; PR lookups serialize per session with `SequencerByKey`. Different sessions remain independent and concurrent.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A verified current branch association avoids network lookup; restricted mode records successful positive and negative resolutions keyed by checkout/candidate inputs. Git-state probing still runs before either cache can short-circuit. OctoKit uses ETag revalidation rather than a no-request warm hit.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed outcome predicate, unconditional refresh-before-lookup, subprocess implementation, and test covering all three outcomes are direct.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Repository size, git probe duration, and cancellation/error frequency vary; this affects severity, not reachability of the added subprocess work.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated subprocess work: the diff newly runs the full attachment path after cancellation and error even when no relevant state changed.

Scenarios.Scenario: The automatic pull-request association setting or experiment assignment changes while several sessions are resident.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The setting update itself does not await reconciliation, but all queued session lookups start immediately in the background; each session's branch lookup precedes its optional SHA fallback.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: GitHub branch lookup and optional exact-HEAD pull-request lookup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: For N cold eligible sessions, N branch GETs and up to N additional commit GETs. Default residency permits 10 sessions; held/subscribed sessions can increase N.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Root configuration changes did not trigger pull-request discovery across all sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the setting UI critical path, but aggregate requests contend for network/API quota and determine when session actions become available.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve exact HEAD using `git rev-parse` after a branch lookup miss.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to one subprocess per cold session whose branch lookup misses.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before that session's SHA fallback can proceed; concurrent across session keys.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of resident sessions with ready non-base branches and no reusable association; normal bounded cardinality is up to 10, with exceptions for held/subscribed sessions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Only same-session work is sequenced. The loop starts all distinct session keys without a shared limiter, so effective aggregate concurrency is N.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Current verified associations and empty restricted candidate sets short-circuit. Cold distinct branch routes do not share cache entries; OctoKit ETags help only after the exact route has already been requested and do not coalesce concurrent requests.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all-session enumeration, per-key-only sequencing, and the exact branch/SHA fallback chain are established in code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The fraction of resident sessions that are eligible and cold depends on usage, but ten resident sessions is an explicit normal configuration.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable concurrency burst: the new listener fans setting changes into unbounded aggregate per-session boundary work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restricted mode reconciles agent-recorded PR artifacts or explicitly associated PRs after artifacts, branch state, or PR status changes.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Reconciliation is background work. Candidate filtering and cached-resolution checks run synchronously before authentication/network; branch lookup then optional SHA fallback are sequential.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch up to 100 pull requests for a branch to select among allowed candidate URLs; optionally query commit-associated PRs after a miss.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one branch request plus one SHA request per changed checkout/candidate resolution; repeated unchanged successful or negative resolutions make zero requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Restricted candidate reconciliation did not exist; automatic lookup requested only one most-recent branch result.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Determines when the restricted actionable association updates, but is off unrelated session progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One only when the allowed branch lookup finds no candidate and a working directory exists.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The previous automatic checkout resolver used the same branch-miss `rev-parse` fallback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks the SHA fallback for this reconciliation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective candidate count is distinct recorded GitHub PR artifacts plus associated URLs. Associated history is bounded to 10; artifact storage is not explicitly bounded but typical sessions record few PR artifacts.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Per-session requests serialize; separate sessions are concurrent. Candidate selection itself is local linear work over artifacts and returned items.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Resolver caches both successful selection and successful absence while checkout/artifact/candidate inputs remain unchanged. It invalidates on artifact and setting changes and cleans entries on session removal. OctoKit keeps 100 ETag/body entries; failures are not negative-cached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the call path and caching; uncertain prevalence of large branch histories.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Branches with many historical PRs can make the `per_page=100` response larger, but common cardinality and a semantics-preserving narrower existing API were not established strongly enough for a separate finding.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding beyond the reported triggering paths: the restricted resolver coalesces unchanged inputs and owns cleanup, while the larger branch response is required by current candidate-selection semantics.

Scenarios.Scenario: A session is created from the PR picker or restored with automatic attachment enabled.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: PR-picker metadata construction is local and synchronous. Session restoration launches attachment fire-and-forget after restoration; its git refresh and GitHub lookup are not required for restore completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing automatic branch lookup and optional SHA fallback during restored-session attachment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero for the picker metadata helper itself; restored cold sessions perform one branch GET and possibly one commit GET.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Restored sessions already invoked attachment and the resolver extraction preserves automatic-mode boundary count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off restore completion because the attachment promise is not awaited.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected PR per picker-created session; one attachment per restored session.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Restores can run across sessions; each session's PR lookup is sequenced. Picker metadata performs no asynchronous work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The picker now marks its selected URL as associated, allowing restricted mode to trust it without a lookup. Automatic-mode restore retains OctoKit ETag behavior and current-branch short-circuiting.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed picker code only constructs bounded metadata and the restored-session attach call is pre-existing.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Restore concurrency depends on client workflow, but this diff does not increase automatic-mode restore boundary count.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression: picker provenance is metadata-only, and automatic-mode resolver extraction preserves the prior lookup sequence.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 16 changed files. Reported two diff-caused regressions: repeated git subprocess work after cancelled/errored turns, and an aggregate network/subprocess burst when the new setting changes across resident sessions. Reviewed restricted-candidate caching, ETag behavior, resolver cleanup, picker provenance, and restore behavior; no other high-confidence performance issue or regression fix was established.
